{
  "feasibility": {
    "verdict": "partially_feasible",
    "answerable": [
      "Simulate natural recharge and unsaturated-zone soil moisture / water-table dynamics under 1980-2018 climate forcing at representative agricultural sites",
      "Provide the recharge boundary condition and vadose-zone water storage response that would drive a coupled subsurface (PFLOTRAN) groundwater model",
      "Bracket the relative sensitivity of water-table position to reduced net groundwater extraction via prescribed sink-term scenarios"
    ],
    "not_answerable": [
      "Absolute basin-wide water-level recovery magnitude, because observed agricultural pumping records are missing and cannot be reconstructed reliably",
      "Lateral groundwater flow, well interference, and aquifer transmissivity effects are not represented by single-column ELM alone (requires PFLOTRAN 3D)",
      "Precise 30% reduction impact without calibrated pumping baseline; only scenario-relative differences can be estimated"
    ]
  },
  "n_columns": 3,
  "n_justification": "Three columns capture the basin's land-cover and topographic gradient: upland cropland recharge zone, mid-slope agricultural, and lowland/riparian discharge area near the Upper Iowa River. This spans the elevation range (260-420 m) and dominant agricultural soils controlling recharge that feeds the shallow aquifer, sufficient for a site-archetype pumping-scenario study while keeping computation tractable.",
  "columns": [
    {
      "id": "upland_cropland",
      "lat": 43.62,
      "lon": -92.35,
      "soil_texture": "silty_clay_loam"
    },
    {
      "id": "midslope_ag",
      "lat": 43.45,
      "lon": -91.85,
      "soil_texture": "silt_loam"
    },
    {
      "id": "lowland_riparian",
      "lat": 43.30,
      "lon": -91.40,
      "soil_texture": "loam"
    }
  ],
  "elm_config": {
    "DATM_CLMNCEP_YR_START": "1980",
    "DATM_CLMNCEP_YR_END": "2018",
    "STOP_N": "10",
    "RUN_STARTDATE": "2009-01-01",
    "hist_variables": [
      "QDRAI",
      "QRECHARGE",
      "QOVER",
      "QRUNOFF",
      "ZWT",
      "WA",
      "H2OSOI",
      "SOILLIQ",
      "SOILICE",
      "RAIN",
      "SNOW",
      "QINFL",
      "QCHARGE",
      "TWS",
      "FGR",
      "TSOI"
    ]
  },
  "requires_capabilities": [
    "ELM-PFLOTRAN coupling for saturated-zone groundwater flow and prescribed pumping sink terms",
    "PFLOTRAN 3D subsurface flow domain parameterized with aquifer hydraulic conductivity/storativity",
    "Scenario management interface to prescribe baseline vs 30%-reduced extraction rates",
    "USGS well time-series ingestion for water-level calibration/validation"
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "Missing pumping records are proxied by literature/USGS-estimated county-level agricultural withdrawal rates for the Upper Iowa (HUC 07060002); results are relative not absolute",
    "10-year evaluation period (2009-2018) uses recent forcing to reflect current climate; a spin-up cycling of 1980-2008 forcing establishes equilibrium water table before scenario runs",
    "Baseline extraction assumed steady seasonal (growing-season) sink; the 30% reduction is applied uniformly to the growing-season pumping flux",
    "ELM provides recharge (QRECHARGE/QCHARGE) as the top boundary flux to PFLOTRAN; lateral aquifer dynamics handled entirely by PFLOTRAN",
    "Soil textures assigned from SSURGO/gridded soil databases for the mapped column locations",
    "Water-level 'recovery' quantified as difference in simulated water-table depth (ZWT / PFLOTRAN head) between reduced-pumping and baseline scenarios over the decade"
  ]
}

answerable: Simulate natural recharge and unsaturated-zone soil moisture / water-table dynamics under 1980-2018 climate forcing at representative agricultural sites
Provide the recharge boundary condition and vadose-zone water storage response that would drive a coupled subsurface (PFLOTRAN) groundwater model
Bracket the relative sensitivity of water-table position to reduced net groundwater extraction via prescribed sink-term scenarios
not_answerable: Absolute basin-wide water-level recovery magnitude, because observed agricultural pumping records are missing and cannot be reconstructed reliably
Lateral groundwater flow, well interference, and aquifer transmissivity effects are not represented by single-column ELM alone (requires PFLOTRAN 3D)
Precise 30% reduction impact without calibrated pumping baseline; only scenario-relative differences can be estimated

parsed.n_justification: Three columns capture the basin's land-cover and topographic gradient: upland cropland recharge zone, mid-slope agricultural, and lowland/riparian discharge area near the Upper Iowa River. This spans the elevation range (260-420 m) and dominant agricultural soils controlling recharge that feeds the shallow aquifer, sufficient for a site-archetype pumping-scenario study while keeping computation tractable.
requires_capabilities: ELM-PFLOTRAN coupling for saturated-zone groundwater flow and prescribed pumping sink terms
PFLOTRAN 3D subsurface flow domain parameterized with aquifer hydraulic conductivity/storativity
Scenario management interface to prescribe baseline vs 30%-reduced extraction rates
USGS well time-series ingestion for water-level calibration/validation
assumptions: Missing pumping records are proxied by literature/USGS-estimated county-level agricultural withdrawal rates for the Upper Iowa (HUC 07060002); results are relative not absolute
10-year evaluation period (2009-2018) uses recent forcing to reflect current climate; a spin-up cycling of 1980-2008 forcing establishes equilibrium water table before scenario runs
Baseline extraction assumed steady seasonal (growing-season) sink; the 30% reduction is applied uniformly to the growing-season pumping flux
ELM provides recharge (QRECHARGE/QCHARGE) as the top boundary flux to PFLOTRAN; lateral aquifer dynamics handled entirely by PFLOTRAN
Soil textures assigned from SSURGO/gridded soil databases for the mapped column locations
Water-level 'recovery' quantified as difference in simulated water-table depth (ZWT / PFLOTRAN head) between reduced-pumping and baseline scenarios over the decade
